name: Eka
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: No published description of Eka (sino1245, no ISO) located; Glottolog page shows no descriptive references.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; stub citing Yang 2010 only (autonym o21 kha24, exonym Menghua, 3,000 speakers in Yijiacun, Heliu, Shuangjiang).

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2015. Lalo dialects across time and space: subgrouping, dialectometry, and intelligibility. (Asia-Pacific Linguistics 22.) Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics, ANU. (Eka sketch = §3.4, pp. 46–50.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Published revision of the thesis; the Eka sketch (§3.4, pp. 46–50) is essentially the same text: tonal system, phonation, tone sandhi; no statement on word stress. The only 'stressed syllable' sentence (p. 40) concerns CW-QY, not Eka.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2011. ISO 639-3 change request 2011-096: create code element 'Eka' [ekb] (rejected 2012-03-28). SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; location (Yijiazhai, Mengmeng Town, Shuangjiang County; N23°28'30" E99°51'54"), 3,000 speakers, classification Ngwi > Central > Lalo, unintelligible with other Lalo varieties, 1,001-item wordlist recorded; cites Yang & Chan 2008 and Yang 2010 as the only sources.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2008. Eka (Yijiacun) 1,001-item wordlist recordings and Levenshtein/intelligibility data (SIL East Asia Group / La Trobe fieldwork; Excel data file 33403_SOURCE4_2_A.xlsx attached to the OPAL thesis record).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Primary data behind the sketch; the OPAL record's xlsx/zip attachments (https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/38767287.) may hold the transcribed Eka wordlist but will carry tone numerals, not stress; useful only for an instrumental check of prominence.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2010. Lalo regional varieties: phylogeny, dialectometry, and sociolinguistics. PhD thesis, La Trobe University, Melbourne. 447 pp. (Eka phonological sketch = §3.4, pp. 74–79.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about stress in Eka. §3.4 (pp. 74–79) gives Eka's syllable template (C)V(N)TP / NT with 6 tones x harsh/modal phonation, the tone reflexes of Proto-Lalo, and extensive tone sandhi (high tone 55 word-medial, 53 word-final; low 21 > 33 before low; 24 > 35 before low). Whole-text a full-text search for stress/accent/prominen/unstressed: the only 'stressed syllable' remark (p. 64) is about the Central Lalo variety CW-QY (Qingyun village), not Eka.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid Eka (ekaa1234) and reference records 70710, 318297. Hammarström et al.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; lists only Yang 2010 (phonology, Glottolog's most extensive description) and Chan & Yang 2008 (a wordlist or less); classification Lalo (lalo1240); note that Eka is unintelligible to all other Lalo varieties.

sources.citation: Lexibank varieties 'yangyi-Eka' and 'yanglalo-Yijiacun' (Yang's Ngwi/Lalo wordlists, CLDF).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist/segment inventories with tone numerals only; no stress marking or statement.

sources.citation: Chan, Catherine Ching Yee & Cathryn Yang. 2008. The Eka language: a first look. Paper presented at ICSTLL 41, SOAS, London, 18–21 September 2008.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only other first-hand description of Eka (the survey presentation on which the thesis sketch is based); Glottolog holds it as a 1-page item, so it most likely also stops at segments and tones, but it is the sole remaining primary item to check.

sources.citation: Björverud, Sofia. 1998. A grammar of Lalo. (Travaux de l'Institut de Linguistique de Lund 35.) Lund: Lund University.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only
sources.note: Fullest grammar of any Lalo variety (Central Lalo of western Weishan, xish1235 — NOT Eka, which is unintelligible with it); its phonology chapter is the place a stress remark for the Lalo cluster would exist, and would serve only as a related-variety proxy with an explicit identity caveat.
